title: Directory size setattr regression
scope: C++ Namespace path setters and inode RPC only; no native FSKit compatibility claim
change: A present size attribute on a directory is rejected with EISDIR after attribute validation, mutability/protection checks, and the existing symlink-size check, but before no-op shortcuts. Existing validation and protection error precedence is preserved.

baseline.observed: Both baseline runs stopped at the size-only zero case: C++ failed its EISDIR assertion, and raw inode-setattr returned wire success with the directory stat. The baseline did not reach the nonzero assertions.

covered_cases: C++ set_attributes and set_link_attributes: root, child directory, and nested child; size-only zero/nonzero and mixed size/mode/times/flags; exact EISDIR
C++ failures preserve committed sequence, inode fields, and directory entries
Directory metadata-only update succeeds; set_attributes follows a symlink to a directory and returns EISDIR for size
C++ set_link_attributes preserves existing symlink-size rejection behavior
Regular file truncate to size zero succeeds
Raw inode-setattr, inode-setattr-times, and inode-setattr-flags: size-only and mixed size/mode/time/flags at zero/nonzero; exact errno+1 EISDIR and unchanged sequence/inode/parent entry
Directory fixture verification, garbage collection, and reopen verification

execution_controls.environment: isolated HOME and TMP; loopback-only execution

limitations: The baseline failure was directly observed for size zero; nonzero behavior is covered by the fixed suite but was not independently run against the baseline runtime.
The results establish the C++ Namespace and inode RPC behavior only. FSKit-enabled build success is not native mount acceptance, and no native FSKit call behavior is claimed.
Existing attribute validation, read-only, immutable, append-only, and symlink-size error precedence remains in force before the directory EISDIR guard.
